record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Well-posedness for delayed model with nonlocal spatial reaction term
record.original_question: For the one-dimensional delayed model ∂_t u = D1 u_xx + D2 ∂_x(u ∂_x u_τ) + f(u, ū), where ū is the spatial average of u over the domain and the boundary condition is homogeneous Neumann, under what conditions does a unique solution exist? What changes in higher spatial dimensions or under other boundary conditions?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 25. Under what conditions does there exist a unique solution solving problem (2.21) subject to a homogeneous Neumann boundary condition? What about in higher spatial dimensions or other boundary conditions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = (a,b) \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a bounded interval and let $\tau > 0$ be a fixed time delay. For a function $u : [-\tau,\infty) \times \overline{\Omega} \to \mathbb{R}$, denote by $u_\tau(t,x) := u(t-\tau,x)$ the time-delayed state, and by
$$\bar u(t) := \frac{1}{|\Omega|} \int_\Omega u(t,y)\,dy$$
the spatial average of $u(t,\cdot)$ over $\Omega$. Consider the nonlinear, nonlocal, delayed parabolic problem
$$\partial_t u(t,x) = D_1\, \partial_{xx} u(t,x) + D_2\, \partial_x\!\big(u(t,x)\, \partial_x u_\tau(t,x)\big) + f\big(u(t,x),\,\bar u(t)\big),\qquad t>0,\ x\in\Omega,$$
with diffusion constants $D_1>0$, $D_2 \in \mathbb{R}$, a given sufficiently regular reaction nonlinearity $f:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$, homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions
$$\partial_x u(t,a) = \partial_x u(t,b) = 0,\qquad t>0,$$
and a prescribed history $u(s,x) = \varphi(s,x)$ for $s\in[-\tau,0]$, $x\in\Omega$, where $\varphi$ belongs to a suitable function space.

(a) Determine conditions on the data $(D_1, D_2, f, \tau, \varphi)$ under which this initial-boundary value problem admits a unique (classical or weak) solution, globally or at least locally in time.

(b) Investigate the corresponding well-posedness question when $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is a bounded domain with $n\ge 2$ (with the gradient and divergence replacing the one-dimensional derivatives, so the cross-diffusion term becomes $D_2\,\nabla\!\cdot(u\,\nabla u_\tau)$), and when the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition is replaced by other boundary conditions (e.g.\ Dirichlet, Robin, or periodic).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem about well-posedness for a delayed cross-diffusion model with nonlocal (spatial-average) reaction term. No published proof of existence/uniqueness in this precise setting was located; related results exist for memory-based diffusion PDEs but not for this exact delayed nonlocal system.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 25: existence and uniqueness for the one-dimensional delayed model with nonlocal reaction and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, with extensions to higher dimensions or other boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem.
